import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 3

def design(feats):
    # Find features with strong effect sizes (|mean_y1-mean_y0| > 0.2)
    effect_sizes = [abs(feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)] > 0].mean() - 
                       feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)] <= 0].mean()) 
                   for fid in feats.ids]
    
    # Get top candidates by effect size
    top_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1][:10]
    candidates = [feats.ids[i] for i in top_indices if effect_sizes[i] > 0.2]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (correlated features)
    filtered_candidates = []
    for fid in candidates:
        is_duplicate = False
        for existing_fid in filtered_candidates:
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(existing_fid)])[0,1]) > 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            filtered_candidates.append(fid)
    
    # If no strong candidates, return empty design
    if len(filtered_candidates) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Try product terms between top candidates
    best_score = -np.inf
    best_drivers = ()
    best_columns = ()
    best_products = ()
    best_loadings = {}
    
    # Check all pairs for product terms
    for i in range(min(len(filtered_candidates), 3)):
        for j in range(i+1, min(len(filtered_candidates), 3)):
            a, b = filtered_candidates[i], filtered_candidates[j]
            # Create product feature
            product_vals = feats.x[:, feats.column(a)] * feats.x[:, feats.column(b)]
            
            # Test if product improves model performance
            X_test = feats.x[:, [feats.column(f) for f in [a,b]]]
            y = feats.y
            
            # Use mutual information to rank features
            mi_scores = mutual_info_classif(X_test, y)
            selected_cols = [a,b][np.argsort(mi_scores)[::-1][:2]]
            
            # Try logistic regression with both features and their product
            X = np.column_stack([feats.x[:, feats.column(f)] for f in selected_cols])
            if len(selected_cols) == 2:
                X = np.column_stack([X, product_vals])
                
            # Fit simple logistic regression to estimate effect
            try:
                lr = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', C=0.1)
                lr.fit(X, y)
                score = lr.score(X, y)
                if score > best_score:
                    best_score = score
                    best_drivers = (a, b) if len(selected_cols) == 2 else ()
                    best_columns = tuple(selected_cols)
                    best_products = ((a,b),) if len(selected_cols) == 2 else ()
                    # Simple loading based on coefficient magnitude
                    best_loadings = {fid: abs(coef) for fid, coef in zip(selected_cols, lr.coef_[0])}
            except:
                continue
    
    # If no good interaction found, use single strongest feature
    if not best_products:
        # Select single strongest feature by effect size
        strongest_fid = filtered_candidates[0]
        return Design(
            drivers=(strongest_fid,),
            columns=(strongest_fid,),
            products=(),
            loadings={strongest_fid: 1.0}
        )
    
    return Design(
        drivers=best_drivers,
        columns=best_columns,
        products=best_products,
        loadings=best_loadings
    )
